The test image shows a corn ear with:
- Pink/rose-colored discoloration on kernels at one end
- Some kernels appear swollen, wrinkled, and brownish-pink
- Dark/black areas near the silk/shank end
- Normal yellow kernels at the other end

This points toward an ear rot. The pink coloration is key — candidates are Gibberella (pink at tip), Fusarium (scattered pink/salmon), or Diplodia (white at base). Let me check reference images.
The Gibberella reference shows dark, mummified ears externally. Let me check one more to differentiate from Fusarium clearly.

**Analysis summary:**

**Test image observations:**
- Corn ear with husks pulled back
- Pink/rose-colored discolored kernels concentrated at the **tip end** (where brown dried silks are visible)
- Some kernels appear dark/black in the most severely affected region
- Normal yellow kernels on the opposite end (base)
- No olive-green, dark-green, or white cottony mold visible

**Differential reasoning:**
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Pink-red mold at the **tip** starting from the silk channel — matches perfectly (concentrated pink at tip, silk entry point visible)
- **Fusarium**: Scattered pink/salmon cottony mold with starburst pattern on individual kernels — doesn't match (not scattered, no white cottony texture)
- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: White mold starting at the **base** — doesn't match (wrong color, wrong location)
- **Ear_rots_Aspergillus/Trichoderma**: Olive-green/dark-green mold — doesn't match (wrong color)

The pink discoloration concentrated at the ear tip (silk channel entry point) is the hallmark of Gibberella ear rot, consistent with infection via the silk channel.
